s.note: Chilled prawns in Marie Rose on crisp iceberg. One word: plastics.
s.how: Stir the mayo, tomato sauce, Worcestershire, Tabasco and a squeeze of lemon into a pink sauce. Divide the lettuce and avocado between 4 glasses. Pile on the prawns and spoon over the sauce. Dust with paprika and hang a lemon wedge on each glass.

s.note: Lemony crab on cool cucumber rounds with dill. Just drifting in the pool.
s.how: Mix the crab with the creme fraiche, lemon zest, a squeeze of juice, dill and pepper. Cut the cucumbers into thick rounds and scoop a small hollow in each. Spoon in the crab. Top each with a few beads of roe.

m.n: Mr. Gladstone's room service steak Diane
m.note: Seared fillet steaks in a mushroom cream pan sauce. Signed in at the Taft as Gladstone.
m.how: Bake the potato chips with a little oil at 220C until crisp. Sear the seasoned steaks in the oil until done to your liking, then rest. Melt the butter and cook the shallots and mushrooms until golden. Add the brandy and let it bubble off, then stir in the mustard, Worcestershire and cream. Return the steaks with their juices, scatter with parsley and serve with the chips.

m.note: Char-grilled beef burger with cheddar and fries. A drive-in talk at last.
m.how: Bake the fries at 220C until crisp. Shape the mince into 4 patties and season well. Grill over high heat, adding the cheese for the last minute. Build the toasted buns with sauce, lettuce, tomato, onion and patty, and serve with the fries.

w.note: White vanilla sponge with lemon curd and cream. Elaine runs out on her own wedding.
w.how: Beat the butter and sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs one at a time. Fold in the flour, vanilla and milk and split between 2 lined 20cm tins. Bake at 180C until springy, then cool. Whip the cream with the icing sugar, spread the curd and half the cream between the layers, and cover the top with the rest.

d.note: Bourbon on the rocks with a twist of orange. Mrs. Robinson pours.
d.how: Put a large ice cube in each of 4 short glasses and pour over 60ml bourbon. Twist a strip of orange peel over each glass and drop it in.
